explanation: In Anglo-Saxon England, 240 silver pennies were struck from a pound of silver, which is why the pound held 240 pence until decimalization in 1971.

claims.text: The pound sterling originally meant the value of a pound weight of silver.
The pound sterling did not begin as a pound weight of gold, copper or bronze.
In Anglo-Saxon England, 240 silver pennies were made from a pound of silver.
The pound was divided into 240 pence until decimalization in February 1971.
